requestedActions.title: List active task titles from the connected Todoist account, including paginated results

guide.summary: Todoist documents OAuth with authorization code flow, PKCE S256, and dynamic client registration. For listing active task titles, the documented read-only grant data:read covers tasks, and GET /api/v1/tasks is documented with cursor pagination until next_cursor is null. Client registration, consent, and token exchange are setup requirements. Provider review, marketplace distribution, and customer-admin approval for other workspaces are not covered by the supplied sources and remain unknown. Setup and execution are untested.

findings.title: OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE and dynamic client registration
findings.detail: The authorization endpoint accepts scope and response_type=code. Redirect users to the authorization URL. The metadata lists dynamic client registration, the authorization_code and refresh_token grants, and S256 PKCE. Setup requires registering the app and configuring redirect URIs, which is a first-test prerequisite.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. It is the least-privilege documented grant for listing active tasks. It also exposes projects, labels, and filters, which is broader than tasks alone, but no narrower documented read grant covers the request.
findings.appliesWhen: Always for this read-only task listing request.

findings.title: Cursor pagination through the task list
findings.detail: Fetch the first page without a cursor using limit, then pass next_cursor as cursor on subsequent requests. Keep the same parameters across pages. Continue until next_cursor is null. The page and offset parameters are not supported.
findings.appliesWhen: Required for paginated listing of active task titles.

steps.detail: Register the app through Todoist's documented dynamic client registration and configure a developer-owned redirect URI. Store client_id and client_secret only if the registration returns them. No registration is claimed until the provider returns it.
steps.doneWhen: A client_id is recorded and the redirect URI matches the callback used in the authorization request. Registration is not assumed to have succeeded before the response is received.

steps.title: Authorize with data:read and exchange the code for an access token
steps.detail: Send the connecting individual customer to the authorization URL with scope=data:read, response_type=code, a state value and a PKCE S256 code challenge. After consent, exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using the documented OAuth token headers. The code and access token are returned at runtime and are not assumed.
steps.doneWhen: Customer consent returns an authorization code and the token exchange returns an access token. No consent is claimed before the redirect completes.

steps.title: List the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with limit=50 and no cursor, sending the access token from the setup step in the Authorization Bearer header. Representative input: ACCESS_TOKEN from the token exchange. Expected result: a 200 response with a results array and a next_cursor value. Collect the content property of each results object as the task title, and read next_cursor for continuation. Boundary check: confirm the token carries only data:read, which grants read-only access, and make no create, update, complete or delete call. Stop if a permission error appears. Do not claim a narrower grant, because data:read also exposes projects, labels and filters.
steps.doneWhen: A 200 response returns results and next_cursor, and task content values are collected. If next_cursor is null the listing ends on this page; otherwise run the continuation step. Only GET requests were made.

steps.title: Fetch the next task page using next_cursor
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with limit=50 and cursor set to the next_cursor value from the prior response. Keep other parameters identical and use the same Bearer token. Representative input: NEXT_CURSOR from the prior page. Expected result: a 200 response with results and next_cursor. Do not use page or offset, which this API version does not support. Boundary check: stay on the data:read grant and make only GET requests; do not treat two pages as a complete listing.
steps.doneWhen: Each page returns results and next_cursor. Keep repeating until next_cursor is null, the documented end of results, then report all collected task content values across pages.
